mainTopic: Slaughtering the קרבן פסח for someone still טמא on ערב פסח: רב and עולא on the טמא שרץ, the זב and זבה, and why a נדה qualifies only on her eighth day
overview: This amud opens with the end of רב's ruling: we may not slaughter the קרבן פסח for a טמא שרץ, while עולא says we may. The גמרא works out רב's principle. A טבול יום is included because the sun sets by itself. A מחוסר כפורים is included because his birds are ready, or already handed to the כהנים, whom we trust like רב שמעיה. A טמא שרץ is excluded because he still has to immerse himself. A contradiction with another ruling of רב leads the גמרא to say that, for רב, a טמא שרץ is unfit by Torah law. The proof is the desert טמאים on their seventh day, following רבי יצחק. The גמרא then defends רב from a משנה about a זב on his seventh day, and debates whether the זב there had already immersed. Next, a ברייתא saying we slaughter for a זבה (or, in רבינא's version, a נדה) on her seventh day is corrected to 'eighth day.' For the נדה, the point is that she immerses only at night after seven full days. The amud ends as a new משנה about an אונן begins.

steps.title: רב excludes the טמא שרץ, עולא includes him
steps.stepSummary: רב's ruling ends: no שחיטה or זריקה for a טמא שרץ. עולא disagrees and says we do slaughter and sprinkle even for a טמא שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not slaughter the פסח and sprinkle its blood on behalf of a person who is טמא from a שרץ. And עולא said: we do slaughter and sprinkle even on behalf of a טמא שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רב's ruling. רב leaves out the טמא שרץ. Then it quotes עולא, who disagrees and includes him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא שרץ can go to the מקוה that day and be טהור by night, in time to eat the פסח. Even so, רב says we cannot slaughter for him while he is still טמא. עולא says his ability to become טהור by night is enough, so we slaughter for him too.

keyTerms.meaning: We slaughter (here, the קרבן פסח)
We sprinkle (the blood on the מזבח)
A person made impure by touching a dead creeping creature. He needs טבילה and sunset to become pure.
Even / also

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of רב's statement. The words 'ואין שוחטין' are the end of רב's ruling, which began on the previous amud (where he allowed a טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים). They are not a new anonymous statement.

phrases.english: And we do not slaughter and sprinkle
phrases.notes: This is still part of רב's ruling.

phrases.english: on behalf of one impure from a creeping creature.
And Ulla said:
We even slaughter and sprinkle
on behalf of one impure from a creeping creature.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוּלָּא אָמַר: אַף שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's ruling on the previous amud and presents עולא's opposing view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: no שחיטה or זריקה for a טמא שרץ. עולא: we do slaughter and sprinkle even for a טמא שרץ.

steps.title: Why is the טבול יום different from the טמא שרץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רב: you allow a טבול יום because he will be fit at night. But a טמא שרץ will also be fit at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, what is different about a טבול יום? That he is fit at night? A טמא שרץ is also fit at night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's line. It points out that the reason he gave for including a טבול יום seems to apply to a טמא שרץ too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason we slaughter for a טבול יום is that he will be able to eat by nightfall. A טמא שרץ can also be ready by nightfall if he goes to the מקוה today. So why does רב treat them differently?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (a formula asking for the distinction between two cases)
Someone who already went to the מקוה today and only waits for sunset to be fully טהור
Is fit / is eligible
At night / by evening
Also / too

phrases.english: According to Rav, what is different about one who immersed today
— that he is fit at night?
One impure from a creeping creature also
is fit at night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רב drew in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's distinction between a טבול יום (included) and a טמא שרץ (excluded)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'fit by nightfall' is the reason, it applies to a טמא שרץ equally, so the distinction collapses

steps.title: The טמא שרץ still lacks immersion
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the טמא שרץ is still missing טבילה. He has not yet done the action he needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is missing immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. The טמא שרץ is different because he still has to go to the מקוה, and he has not gone yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'fit at night' is not enough. The טבול יום already did his טבילה, but the טמא שרץ still has to do it himself. Since that action is still undone, we cannot slaughter on his behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking / missing (something still needed)
Immersion in a מקוה
Someone who still needs to immerse

phrases.english: He lacks immersion.
phrases.notes: A short answer, and it's talking about the person who is טמא from a שרץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by what step is still missing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both are equally 'fit at night,' so they should be treated alike
steps.terutzMaskana: The טמא שרץ still needs to do an action (טבילה), so he is excluded

steps.title: The טבול יום also lacks something: sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the טבול יום is also still missing something, the sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טבול יום is also missing something: the setting of the sun!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 3. It points out that the טבול יום is also not finished, because he still needs sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'still missing something' disqualifies a person, the טבול יום should be disqualified too. He is not fully טהור until the sun sets. So the answer seems to knock out the טבול יום as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset, which completes the purification of a טבול יום
Still waiting for sunset
Ritual purity

phrases.english: One who immersed today also —
lacks the setting of the sun!

steps.triggerLanguage: טְבוּל יוֹם נָמֵי מְחוּסָּר הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that 'something still missing' disqualifies a person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טבול יום is also incomplete until sunset, so by that principle he too should be excluded

steps.title: The sun sets by itself
steps.stepSummary: Answer: sunset happens automatically. No action is needed from the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sun sets on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the answer. What disqualifies a person is a missing action he must do. Sunset is not an action; it comes by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is now clearer. Missing טבילה is a problem because the person has to go and do it. Missing sunset is no problem, because it will surely happen without any effort from him.

keyTerms.meaning: The sun
By itself / automatically
Sets (goes down)

phrases.english: The sun sets by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by refining the principle
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the principle: only a missing action disqualifies, not a missing automatic event
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any missing element, even sunset, disqualifies
steps.terutzMaskana: Sunset comes automatically, so the טבול יום is included. Only a missing action (like טבילה) excludes.

steps.title: The מחוסר כפורים still lacks an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a מחוסר כפורים still has to bring his כפרה offering. That is an action, so why does רב include him?
steps.simpleTranslation: A מחוסר כפורים also: he is missing his כפרה!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the refined rule from step 5, the גמרא attacks רב's other case. A מחוסר כפורים still has to bring a קרבן, which is an action he has not done yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר כפורים is someone like a זב or a יולדת who has already immersed and seen sunset but must still bring birds as a קרבן. Bringing a קרבן is an action, not an automatic event. So by the rule of step 5 he should be excluded, yet רב included him.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who still needs to bring an atonement offering to finish his purification (e.g., a זב or a יולדת)
Atonement; here, the offering that completes the purification
But here / behold

phrases.english: One lacking atonement also —
but he is missing his atonement offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים נָמֵי הָא מְחוּסַּר כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the refined principle of step 5 against רב's inclusion of a מחוסר כפורים
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's inclusion of a מחוסר כפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing a קרבן is a required action not yet done. Under the 'missing action' rule, he should be excluded like the טמא שרץ.

steps.title: His birds are already in his hand
steps.stepSummary: Answer: his pair of birds is already in his possession and ready to be brought, so we treat the action as good as done.
steps.simpleTranslation: His pair of birds is in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מחוסר כפורים already has his birds ready. So his missing step is about to happen and is treated as complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His action is not truly missing in practice. The birds are with him, and he can hand them over at once, so we assume he will. The טמא שרץ is different: he still has to go himself to the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'nest': a pair of birds (doves) brought as an offering; 'his nest'
In his hand / in his possession
A man with a discharge-impurity who, if he saw three sightings, must bring birds after purification

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule: we slaughter the פסח for someone still טמא only if no action of his own is still missing. A טבול יום is included because sunset comes by itself. A מחוסר כפורים is included because his birds are already in hand. A טמא שרץ is excluded because he still has to immerse. עולא includes even the טמא שרץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea in the sugya: a person can be counted for the פסח while still טמא, as long as his path to purity is either automatic or ready in hand.

phrases.english: For his nest (pair of birds) is in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: the missing action is immediately available and assumed done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any missing action, even bringing a ready קרבן, disqualifies
steps.terutzMaskana: Since his birds are already in his possession, his כפרה is as good as done, so he is included

steps.title: The impure person can also fix his status right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 3: the טמא שרץ can easily immerse, because a מקוה is right in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one who is impure from a שרץ can also become pure easily. The מקוה is right in front of him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier answer that the טמא שרץ is different because he still needs טבילה. It says immersing is easy and available, so why should that hold him back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the מחוסר כפורים was treated as 'as good as done' because his birds were ready. By the same logic, the טמא שרץ has a מקוה available, so his action should also count as ready. The difference between the two cases seems to disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: A person made impure by touching a dead creeping creature
A ritual bath used for immersion
Behold, it is right in front of him (it is readily available)

phrases.english: One impure from a creeping creature also —
behold, the ritual bath is right in front of him!

steps.triggerLanguage: טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ נָמֵי הֲרֵי מִקְוֶה לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'ready to go' logic of Step 7 to the טמא שרץ, undermining the distinction made in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction that the טמא שרץ is held back because he still lacks טבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If birds that are ready count as done, then an available מקוה should count as done too.

steps.title: He might be careless and not immerse
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that we worry the טמא שרץ might neglect to go to the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he will be careless and not immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even though the מקוה is available, we cannot be sure the person will actually use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether immersing is possible, but whether we can trust it will happen. Since the action depends on the person himself, he might be lazy or forget. So we cannot slaughter the פסח for him on the assumption that he will be pure by evening.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe (expresses a concern)
He was negligent or careless

phrases.english: Perhaps he will be negligent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by introducing a concern about negligence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a practical concern (negligence) that separates the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מקוה is available, the טמא שרץ should count as already pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Availability is not enough. We worry that he will not actually immerse.

steps.title: The same worry should apply to the one lacking atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: then the מחוסר כפורים might also be careless and not bring his birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the one still lacking his atonement offering might also be careless and not bring it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new answer against the מחוסר כפורים case. If we worry about negligence, we should worry about him too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 9 was a worry about negligence. But the מחוסר כפורים also needs to act by bringing his birds, so he too could neglect it. That would mean we should not slaughter for him either, which contradicts the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if that is your reasoning)
Someone who has immersed but still needs to bring his atonement offering

phrases.english: If so, one lacking atonement also —
perhaps he will be negligent!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים נָמֵי דִּילְמָא פָּשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the negligence concern of Step 9 to the מחוסר כפורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that we slaughter for a מחוסר כפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If negligence is a concern, it applies equally to someone who still has to bring an offering.

steps.title: He already handed his birds to the court
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the מחוסר כפורים already gave his birds to the court of כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with a case where he already handed them over to the court of כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. The person has already given his birds to the כהנים, so the action is out of his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry of negligence only applies when the person himself still has to act. Once the birds are with the בית דין of כהנים, his own laziness cannot get in the way. That is why we can slaughter the פסח for him.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; this is a case where (narrows the case)
He handed them over
Court; here, the court of כהנים in the מקדש

phrases.english: For example, where he handed them over to the court,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by limiting the case to one where the offering is already with the כהנים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחוסר כפורים might neglect to bring his offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: His offering is already in the hands of the כהנים, so his own negligence is not a factor.

steps.title: Support from רב שמעיה: the כהנים finish everything the same day
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה taught that the court of כהנים does not leave until all the money in the collection boxes has been used for offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב שמעיה, who said: There is a firm assumption that the court of כהנים does not get up from there until all the money in the collection boxes is used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support that we can trust the כהנים to offer his birds that same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמעיה says the כהנים always use up all the offering money the same day. If they do that with money, they certainly offer actual birds that were handed to them. So we can be sure the מחוסר כפורים will have his atonement by evening.

keyTerms.meaning: A firm presumption that we can rely on
Horn-shaped collection boxes in the מקדש for offering money
Until the money is used up

phrases.english: And this is like Rav Shemaya, who said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה אֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: There is a presumption that the court of priests does not
get up from there
until the money in the collection boxes is used up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 11 by showing the כהנים can be trusted to act that same day.
steps.raayaObject: That birds handed to the בית דין will certainly be offered that day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שמעיה's statement about the court of כהנים using up the collection-box money.
steps.whatToRemember: Under this approach, the טמא שרץ is held back only because of a worry that he will be careless. The מחוסר כפורים is fine because his offering is already in reliable hands.

steps.title: This clashes with רב's other ruling about making someone impure
steps.stepSummary: If a טמא שרץ is fit by Torah law and only רבנן disqualified him, how can רב say we make one person impure with a שרץ to tip the community into a majority of טמאים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב: by Torah law he is fit, and it is only רבנן who made a decree against him. If so, why did רב say: 'We make one of them impure with a שרץ'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a problem with the 'negligence' approach. It makes the טמא שרץ fit by Torah law, which contradicts another ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ruled that when a community is half pure and half impure, we make one more person impure with a שרץ. Then the majority is impure, and the whole community may bring the פסח in טומאה. But if a טמא שרץ is fit by Torah law, he should not count as impure for this purpose, and the plan would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
The Sages made a decree (a rabbinic restriction)
Why then? (introduces a contradiction)
We make (someone) impure

steps.confusionAlert: רב's ruling about making someone impure is a different case: a community split half pure and half impure. Making one person impure turns the community into a majority of טמאים, and then everyone may bring the פסח in טומאה. That only works if a טמא שרץ is truly unfit by Torah law.

phrases.english: And according to Rav, by Torah law he is fit,
and it is the Sages who decreed against him;
why then did Rav say:
'We make one of them impure with a creeping creature'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מִיחְזֵא חֲזֵי וְרַבָּנַן הוּא דִּגְזַרוּ בֵּיהּ אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the negligence-based explanation of Steps 9 to 12 creates a contradiction with another statement of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that a טמא שרץ is unfit only because of a rabbinic decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's ruling about tipping the majority requires the טמא שרץ to be truly impure and unfit by Torah law. A merely rabbinic problem would not change the community's Torah status.

steps.title: For רב, a טמא שרץ is unfit even by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts. According to רב, the טמא שרץ is unfit for the פסח by Torah law, not just by rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, according to רב, by Torah law too he is not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that the problem is only rabbinic. It says that for רב the טמא שרץ is unfit straight from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals a change of approach. The earlier explanation, that we merely worry he will be careless, is set aside for רב. This removes the contradiction with רב's ruling about making someone impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals dropping the previous idea)
He is not fit

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the טמא שרץ has stopped being in the category of someone who can soon become pure. It means that, in his case, the Torah still treats him as unfit for the פסח until he actually becomes pure.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, לְרַב מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא נָמֵי לָא חֲזֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, according to Rav, by Torah law too he is not fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא נָמֵי לָא חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of Step 13 by changing the level of the disqualification from rabbinic to Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טמא שרץ is fit by Torah law and only rabbinically disqualified because of negligence.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב, a טמא שרץ is disqualified by Torah law.

steps.title: Proof from the impure person whose seventh day falls on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a טמא מת includes someone whose seventh day is ערב פסח. He is in the same situation as a טמא שרץ, yet the Torah still pushes him off to פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Any man who is impure from a dead body.' Are we not dealing even with one whose seventh day falls on ערב פסח? That is exactly like the impurity of a שרץ, and still the Torah says he is pushed off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from a פסוק that someone who can become pure that same day is still unfit by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא מת whose seventh day is ערב פסח can be sprinkled and immerse that day and be pure by evening, just as a טמא שרץ can immerse and be pure by evening. Yet the פסוק includes him among those sent to פסח שני. So by Torah law, someone who still needs to act in order to become pure that day is unfit, and this matches רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure from contact with a dead body (טמא מת)
Are we not dealing with (this case too)?
His seventh day, the day of his final sprinkling and immersion
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
He is pushed off (to פסח שני)

steps.whatToRemember: For רב, a טמא שרץ is unfit for the פסח by Torah law. The proof is the טמא מת whose seventh day is ערב פסח: he can become pure that day, yet the Torah defers him. This is also why רב can make one person impure with a שרץ to create a majority of טמאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the level of the disqualification as Torah law. That is what makes רב's practical ruling work, since it lets a community reach a majority of טמאים and bring the פסח in טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶה טָמֵא לָנֶפֶשׁ״.
phrases.english: As it is written: 'Any man who shall be impure from a dead body.'
Are we not dealing with

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחָל שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: one whose seventh day fell on Passover eve,
which is the same as impurity of a creeping creature,
and the Torah said: he is deferred!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶה טָמֵא לָנֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the Torah source for the claim in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a טמא שרץ is unfit for the פסח by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר ט:י, which includes a טמא מת whose seventh day falls on ערב פסח among those deferred to פסח שני.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב, someone who can become pure only by evening, such as a טמא שרץ, is unfit for the פסח by Torah law.

steps.title: How do we know the verse is about people whose seventh day was ערב פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind the claim in Step 15: how do we know the טמאים in the פסוק were people whose seventh day fell on ערב פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will ask: from where do we know that this is so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a question about the proof it just gave. It is setting up the next step, which will give the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the Torah pushed off a טמא מת whose seventh day was ערב פסח. Maybe the פסוק only means someone who was still in the middle of his seven days of impurity. If so, it would teach us nothing about someone who can become pure that same night.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא raises a possible question)

That it is so

phrases.english: And if you will say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the reading of the פסוק used as proof in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we know the טמאים in the desert were people whose seventh day fell on ערב פסח, and not people still in the middle of their impurity.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יצחק: the desert טמאים were on their seventh day
steps.stepSummary: רב holds like רבי יצחק. The טמאים in the desert had become impure from a מת מצוה, and their seventh day fell on ערב פסח. The words 'on that day' show they could have brought it the next day, yet the Torah still pushed them off.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב) holds like רבי יצחק, who said: they were impure from a מת מצוה, and their seventh day fell on ערב פסח. As it says: 'They could not make the פסח on that day.' Only on that day could they not make it, but the next day they could have. And still the Torah said they are pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to רבי יצחק's reading of the פסוק. The people in the desert were on their seventh day and could finish their purification that day, yet the Torah still pushed them off to פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'on that day' (בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא) tell us their problem was only that day. By the next day they would have been pure. So the Torah disqualifies even someone who is almost pure. That is exactly the situation of a טמא שרץ, which supports רב's position that he is disqualified by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: People who became impure by burying an abandoned corpse that had no one else to bury it
The seventh day of purification from טומאת מת
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah
They were pushed off (to פסח שני)

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading is the Torah-level source for רב's view that someone who still has to do an act of purification that day (sprinkling or טבילה), like a טמא שרץ, cannot have the פסח brought for him, even though he could be pure by evening.

They were impure from a met מצוה,

but the next day they can make it,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב follows רבי יצחק. 'On that day' shows the desert טמאים were on their seventh day and would have been pure the next day, yet the Torah still pushed them off.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about a זב on his seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says we slaughter the פסח for a זב who saw two sightings on his seventh day. If that means even before he immerses, then his status matches a טמא שרץ, and we would learn that the פסח may be brought for a טמא שרץ. That contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a זב who saw two sightings, we slaughter for him on his seventh day. Isn't it talking about when he has not yet immersed? Then learn from it that we slaughter and sprinkle the blood for a טמא שרץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to go against רב. It suggests the משנה allows the פסח for someone who has not even immersed yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב on his seventh clean day who has not yet immersed still needs both immersion and sunset. That is the same as a טמא שרץ. If the משנה allows the פסח for him, it should also be allowed for a טמא שרץ, which is the opposite of what רב holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A man made impure by a certain bodily discharge
Two sightings of the discharge (so he needs no קרבן, only seven clean days and immersion)
Isn't it? (the גמרא suggests a reading)
Immersed (in a מקוה)
Sprinkle (the blood on the מזבח)

phrases.english: We learned: a zav who saw two sightings —
we slaughter for him on the seventh day.
Isn't it talking about when he did not immerse,
and learn from it:
we slaughter and sprinkle for a person impure from a sheretz!
phrases.notes: An unimmersed זב on his seventh day is the same as a טמא שרץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having established רב's source, the גמרא now challenges רב from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the פסח cannot be brought for a טמא שרץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה allows the פסח for a זב who has not yet immersed, and his status is the same as a טמא שרץ, then the פסח is allowed for a טמא שרץ too.

steps.title: The משנה is about a זב who already immersed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the משנה is talking about a זב who already immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about when he immersed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reading the משנה differently: the זב already immersed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he has immersed, he is not like a טמא שרץ who still has to immerse. So the משנה tells us nothing about a טמא שרץ, and רב stands.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggested reading)
Where he already immersed

phrases.english: No, it is where he immersed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a זב who has not immersed, which would match a טמא שרץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a זב who already immersed, so it does not apply to a טמא שרץ.

steps.title: If he already immersed, what is the משנה teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the זב already immersed, it seems obvious that we can slaughter for him, so why would the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he immersed, what is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. If the זב already immersed, the משנה's ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he has immersed, he becomes pure at nightfall, before the פסח is eaten. The challenge is that a משנה should teach something new, and this seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (it seems obvious)

phrases.aramaic: אִי טָבֵיל, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן!
phrases.english: If he immersed, what is it teaching us?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי טָבֵיל, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 19 by claiming it makes the משנה say something obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה is about a זב who already immersed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he already immersed, it is obvious that he may have the פסח brought for him, so the משנה would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The new idea: sunset happens by itself
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that even though the זב still lacks sunset, we slaughter for him, because sunset comes on its own and needs no action from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: even though he is still missing sunset, it teaches us that the sun sets by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point the משנה makes about a זב who already immersed. Being 'not yet fully pure' does not block him, because the only thing left is sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that anyone not fully pure at the time of slaughtering is disqualified. The משנה teaches that missing only sunset does not count, since it happens automatically. This differs from a טמא שרץ who has not immersed, because he still has to do something himself, so רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Still missing sunset (the last stage of becoming pure)
The sun sets by itself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, someone who still has to immerse (like a טמא שרץ) cannot have the פסח brought for him by Torah law. Someone who already immersed and only lacks sunset can, because sunset happens on its own.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. The desert טמאים from רבי יצחק and a טמא שרץ still needed to immerse, and they are disqualified. The זב in the משנה already immersed and only needs sunset, and he is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that 'sunset happens by itself' sets up a key line: an action the person still has to do disqualifies him, but a missing step that completes itself does not.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דִּמְחוּסַּר הֶעֱרֵב הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ,
phrases.english: that even though he is still missing sunset,
it teaches us
that the sun sets by itself.
phrases.notes: He needs to do nothing more, so he is treated as ready.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by naming the new idea the משנה teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the חידוש (new idea) of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זב who immersed but lacks sunset might be disqualified because he is not yet fully pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lacking only sunset does not disqualify him, since the sun sets by itself. So the משנה does teach something new, and it does not contradict רב.

steps.title: Support from the last clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says its answer makes sense and brings up the סיפא: a זב who saw three sightings has the פסח slaughtered for him on his eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, since the last part of the משנה teaches: if he saw three sightings, we slaughter for him on the eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof that its answer (the זב had already immersed) is correct. This line only sets up the proof by pointing to the last clause of the משנה. The argument itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the answer that the זב had already immersed only defended רב. Now the גמרא shows that the wording of the משנה itself supports that reading. The evidence is the סיפא about the זב with three sightings.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical. This introduces support for the previous answer.
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Three sightings of זיבה. This makes him a full זב who must bring a קרבן.
The eighth day, when the זב brings his קרבן

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
phrases.notes: This backs up the answer from Step 19.

phrases.english: since the last clause teaches:
if he saw three sightings —
we slaughter for him on the eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for the answer given in Steps 19 and 21
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה's זב with two sightings had already immersed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: a זב with three sightings, slaughtered for on the eighth day

steps.title: If he already immersed, the last clause is needed
steps.stepSummary: If the first clause is about a זב who already immersed, then the סיפא is necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well if you say the זב who saw two sightings, for whom we slaughter on the seventh day, had already immersed. Then the last clause is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the first half of its proof. Under its own reading, the last clause of the משנה has a real purpose. The next step explains what that purpose is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule used here is that a משנה does not include an extra clause for no reason. If the first clause is about someone who already immersed, the סיפא must add something new, and the גמרא is about to show what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well if you say. This introduces the reading that fits.
That he immersed
It is needed. The clause is not extra.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
a zav who saw two sightings
we slaughter for him on the seventh day,
means that he immersed — then [the last clause] is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the argument based on the סיפא introduced in Step 22
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the זב had already immersed
steps.raayaSupportSource: Under this reading, the סיפא is not extra

steps.title: What the last clause teaches: missing a קרבן does not block the פסח
steps.stepSummary: Without the סיפא, we might think only someone who has nothing left to do qualifies. A זב with three sightings still has to bring his קרבן. The סיפא teaches that we slaughter for him anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: only a זב who saw two sightings, on his seventh day, qualifies, because he is not missing any action. But a זב who saw three sightings, on his eighth day, is missing an action, since he still lacks his atonement offering. So he would not qualify. The משנה teaches us that even though he still lacks his atonement offering, we slaughter and sprinkle the blood for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what the last clause adds under its reading. Being מחוסר כפרה does not stop the פסח from being brought for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the two-sighting זב has immersed, he has nothing left to do; only sunset remains, and sunset comes by itself. The three-sighting זב still has to bring a קרבן, which is an action he must do, so we might think he cannot be included. The סיפא tells us that we still slaughter and sprinkle the blood for him.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought. This introduces a mistaken assumption.
Still missing an action he must do
Still missing his atonement קרבן
It teaches us
We sprinkle the blood

steps.confusionAlert: A זב with only two sightings brings no קרבן at all. Only three sightings make him a full זב who must bring a קרבן on the eighth day. That is why only the three-sighting זב is called מחוסר כפרה.

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say,
[only] one who saw two sightings, on the seventh day,
is the one who is not missing an action,
but one who saw three, on the eighth day,
who is missing an action —
he lacks atonement, so no.
It teaches us
that even though he lacks atonement,
we slaughter and sprinkle for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the סיפא is necessary, as claimed in Step 23
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא has a purpose under the reading that he already immersed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The new rule that being מחוסר כפרה does not block the פסח
steps.whyThisMatters: This clarifies a real rule: someone still missing his atonement קרבן can have the פסח slaughtered for him.

steps.title: If he had not immersed, the last clause is unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: Under the other reading, where the two-sighting זב had not yet immersed, the סיפא seems to serve no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the זב who saw two sightings, on the seventh day, had not immersed, why would I need the clause about the one who saw three sightings, on the eighth day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the opposite reading and points out its problem: the last clause becomes extra. The next step shows exactly why it would be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of the proof. A reading that makes part of the משנה pointless is weak, and that pushes us toward the reading that he already immersed.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say. This introduces the reading that does not fit.
That he did not immerse
Why do I need it? This means the clause seems extra.

phrases.english: But if you say
one who saw two sightings, on the seventh day,
means he did not immerse —
why do I need 'he saw three, on the eighth day'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 23 by testing the opposite reading
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the two-sighting זב had not yet immersed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the סיפא would be extra, and a משנה does not include extra clauses

steps.title: A קל וחומר makes the last clause unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: If we slaughter even for a fully impure זב who has not immersed, then surely we slaughter for one who already immersed and whose impurity is weaker. So the סיפא would teach nothing, which proves the first clause is about a זב who already immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now you could say: for one who saw two sightings, on the seventh day, who has not immersed and is fully impure, we slaughter and sprinkle for him. Then for one who saw three, on the eighth day, who already immersed on the seventh and whose impurity is weaker, is it not all the more so that we slaughter and sprinkle for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the last clause would be extra under the non-immersed reading: it would follow from a קל וחומר. This completes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who has not immersed is a טמא מעליא, fully impure. The three-sighting זב on his eighth day has already immersed, so his טומאה is קלישא, weaker. If the משנה allowed the פסח for the more impure person, it would not need to say it allows the פסח for the less impure one. Since the משנה does say it, the first clause must be about a זב who already immersed, which supports the answer that saves רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if so. This introduces a 'how much more so' argument.
Fully impure
Weakened impurity, after immersion
Is it not all the more so?

steps.whatToRemember: The proof goes like this: the סיפא about the three-sighting זב seems to teach something new only if the first clause is about a זב who already immersed. This proof is put forward in Step 27, but Step 28 rejects it. The סיפא can still be needed even if the זב did not immerse (Step 29).

phrases.english: Now it can be said:
one who saw two sightings, on the seventh day,
who did not immerse,
so he is fully impure —
we slaughter and sprinkle for him.
One who saw three, on the eighth day,
who immersed on the seventh day,
so his impurity is weakened —
is it not all the more so
that we slaughter and sprinkle for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the סיפא would be extra, as claimed in Step 25
steps.raayaObject: That the two-sighting זב in the משנה had already immersed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from fully impure to weakened impurity, which would make the סיפא extra under the opposite reading

steps.title: Proposed conclusion that the two-sighting זב had already immersed
steps.stepSummary: Based on the previous argument, the גמרא suggests concluding that the רישא's two-sighting זב, for whom we slaughter on the seventh day, is one who already did טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that the זב who saw two sightings, for whom we slaughter on the seventh day, is one who already immersed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the last few steps and proposes a firm conclusion. Since the סיפא only makes sense if the רישא's זב already immersed, the רישא must be talking about a זב who did טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא showed that if the רישא were about a זב who had not immersed, the סיפא would teach nothing new. A משנה does not include useless clauses, so the גמרא wants to conclude that the רישא is about a זב who already immersed. This conclusion is put forward here and will be tested in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... (introduces a proposed conclusion)
Learn from it; conclude from this
He immersed (in a מקוה)
Sightings of זיבה discharge

phrases.english: Rather, must we not conclude from it:
one who saw two sightings, on the seventh day,
for whom we slaughter, is one who already immersed.
phrases.notes: This is the conclusion the גמרא is driving toward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the argument of step 26 into a proposed conclusion about the case in the רישא.
steps.raayaObject: The רישא (two sightings, seventh day) refers to a זב who already immersed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The need for the סיפא (three sightings, eighth day) to teach something new.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: the two-sighting זב may not have immersed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the conclusion. The רישא can still be about a זב who did not immerse, and the סיפא is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really I can tell you that he did not immerse, and the סיפא is still necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proposed conclusion. It says the רישא could still mean a זב who has not yet immersed, and it will now explain why the סיפא still adds something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that the סיפא would be useless under the 'not immersed' reading. Here the גמרא denies that claim. It promises to show a different reason the סיפא is needed, which is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (keeps the original reading)
It was necessary (to state this clause)

phrases.english: No, really I can say to you
that he did not immerse, and it was still necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion proposed in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the רישא must refer to a זב who already immersed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes the סיפא has no purpose if the רישא's זב did not immerse.

steps.title: Why the סיפא is needed: the זב depends on the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: Without the סיפא we might think the seventh-day זב qualifies because he can fix his status himself by immersing. On the eighth day the three-sighting זב needs the כהנים to bring his קרבן, and they might neglect it. The סיפא teaches that we trust the כהנים, like רב שמעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: on the seventh day he can fix his status himself. But on the eighth day, when he cannot bring the קרבן himself, maybe the כהנים will neglect him. So the סיפא teaches us that the law follows רב שמעיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new reason the סיפא is needed. The difference between the two cases is not how impure the זב is. It is whether the זב can finish his purification by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two-sighting זב only needs to immerse, which is completely in his own hands. The three-sighting זב also needs his קרבן brought, and only the כהנים can do that, so we might worry they will not do it in time. The סיפא teaches, like רב שמעיה, that we rely on the כהנים to bring all the קרבנות, so we may slaughter for him.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say (introduces a mistaken assumption, the הוה אמינא)
It is in his power to fix (his status)
They are negligent
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The סיפא is needed either way. Even if the two-sighting זב did not immerse, the סיפא adds a new point: we trust the כהנים to bring the three-sighting זב's קרבן, like רב שמעיה.
steps.confusionAlert: The סיפא is not adding a case of stronger impurity. It adds a case where the person's purity depends on someone else, the כהנים, rather than on himself.

phrases.english: It might have entered your mind to say
that it is on the seventh day, when it is in his power to fix himself (by immersing),
but on the eighth day, when it is not in his power
to offer the קרבן himself,
say that the כהנים might be negligent with him,
so it teaches us that the law is like רב שמעיה.
phrases.notes: רב שמעיה holds that the כהנים can be relied on to bring all the קרבנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason promised in step 28 for why the סיפא is necessary.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason the clause is needed (חידוש of the סיפא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only someone who can finish purifying himself (by immersing) qualifies. Someone who depends on the כהנים does not, because they might be negligent.
steps.terutzMaskana: We trust the כהנים, like רב שמעיה, so we slaughter for the three-sighting זב on his eighth day.

steps.title: A ברייתא says we slaughter for a זבה on her seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a זבה. A תנא then recites a ברייתא before רב אדא בר אהבה saying we slaughter for a זבה on her seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And a זבה, we slaughter...' A תנא taught before רב אדא בר אהבה: 'And a זבה, we slaughter for her on her seventh day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה about a זבה. It then brings a ברייתא with a surprising wording, which sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says we slaughter for a זבה on her eighth day. This ברייתא says 'seventh day,' which seems to contradict that. The next step questions whether that wording can be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had abnormal bleeding (זיבה)
Before him; in his presence

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'And a זבה, we slaughter, etc.'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: A תנא taught before רב אדא בר אהבה:
'And a זבה, we slaughter for her on her seventh day.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the זב section of the משנה to the זבה section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא says we slaughter the פסח for a זבה on her seventh day.

steps.title: A זבה on her seventh day is not fit to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה objects. Some allow slaughtering for a טמא שרץ, but that person becomes pure by evening. A זבה is not fit until the next day, when she brings her קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is a זבה fit on her seventh day? Even according to the one who says we slaughter and sprinkle for a טמא שרץ, that is only for a טמא שרץ, who is fit by evening. But this זבה is not fit until tomorrow, when she brings her כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges the ברייתא's wording. A זבה on her seventh day cannot eat the פסח that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The most lenient view allows slaughtering only for someone who will be fit to eat that same night, like a טמא שרץ, who immerses and becomes pure at nightfall. A זבה must also bring her קרבן, which is called her כפרה, on the eighth day. So on the night after her seventh day she is still unfit, and we cannot slaughter for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Is she fit? (a rhetorical question meaning 'she is not')
And we sprinkle (the blood)
One made impure by a dead שרץ (creeping creature)
By evening
Atonement; here, the קרבן that completes her purification

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זָבָה בַּשְּׁבִיעִי שֶׁלָּהּ מִי חַזְיָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is a זבה on her seventh day fit?
Even according to the one who says
we slaughter and sprinkle for one impure from a שרץ,
that applies only to one impure from a שרץ
who is fit by evening,
but this one, until tomorrow when she brings her כפרה,
she is not fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that we slaughter for a זבה on her seventh day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We may slaughter only for someone fit to eat that night. A זבה is not fit until her קרבן is brought on the eighth day, so slaughtering on her seventh day is impossible even under the lenient טמא שרץ view.

steps.title: Correcting the ברייתא to read 'eighth day'
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה fixes the text: the ברייתא should say 'her eighth day,' which matches the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'on her eighth day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה solves the problem by correcting the ברייתא's wording from 'seventh' to 'eighth.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: On her eighth day the זבה brings her קרבן and is fully fit that night, so slaughtering for her makes sense. This correction also brings the ברייתא into line with our משנה, which says 'eighth.'

keyTerms.meaning: Say (instead); used to correct a text
On the eighth day

steps.whatToRemember: A זבה is fit for the פסח only from her eighth day, after her קרבן is brought. So the ברייתא is corrected to read 'eighth,' matching the משנה.

phrases.english: Say instead: 'on the eighth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 31 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows slaughtering for a זבה on her seventh day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read 'eighth day,' when the זבה is fully fit.

steps.title: Isn't the eighth-day ruling for a זבה obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the corrected ברייתא, slaughtering for a זבה on her eighth day, teaches nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the corrected ברייתא even needs to tell us this. It seems to repeat what the משנה already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 32 the ברייתא was fixed to say 'eighth day' so it would match the משנה. But if it now just repeats the משנה, it seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what new lesson it contains.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא uses this to object that a statement teaches nothing new.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: Once we fix it to say 'eighth day' for a זבה, that ruling seems too obvious to need teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the corrected text from Step 32 as being redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected ברייתא: slaughter for a זבה on her eighth day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that only repeats a known ruling is pointless, so what does it add?

steps.title: It teaches that we trust the כהנים to bring her offering
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought a זבה still missing her atonement-offering does not qualify. The ברייתא teaches that she does, because we trust the כהנים, like רב שמעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since she is still missing her atonement (her קרבן), no, we do not slaughter for her. So it teaches us that we do, like רב שמעיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling is not obvious. Someone could have worried that her offering would not get brought in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On her eighth day a זבה must still bring a קרבן before she may eat קדשים. We might fear the כהנים will forget, leaving her unfit by evening. The ברייתא teaches that we rely on the כהנים, the same logic used for the זב in Step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a mistaken assumption.
Lacking atonement. Someone who still has to bring a purification קרבן.
It teaches us. This introduces the actual lesson.

phrases.english: You might have said
since she lacks atonement (her offering), no, we do not slaughter for her
phrases.notes: The fear is that her קרבן may not be brought in time.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do, in line with רב שמעיה.
phrases.notes: רב שמעיה: the כהנים can be relied on to bring the offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection of Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a possible mistaken assumption (הוה אמינא) that the teaching rules out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זבה who still owes her קרבן does not qualify, because the כהנים might neglect it.
steps.terutzMaskana: We trust the כהנים (רב שמעיה), so we slaughter for her on the eighth day.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'trust the כהנים' principle covers both the זב (Step 29) and the זבה.

steps.title: רבינא: the ברייתא was really about a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers a different version: the תנא recited a ברייתא about a נדה, saying we slaughter for her on her seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: the תנא recited ‘נדה’ before him: ‘And for a נדה, we slaughter for her on the seventh day.’
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives another version of the story from Step 30. The ברייתא the תנא recited was about a נדה, not a זבה. This sets up a new round of the same discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the case was a זבה. רבינא says the case was a נדה, who has no קרבן to bring. This changes which woman we are discussing, and the next steps work through the same problem for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman made impure by her regular monthly period. She brings no קרבן.
Recited before him. A reciter of ברייתות stated a text in front of a teacher.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new story. רבינא is retelling the same exchange with רב אדא בר אהבה (Steps 30-32), but with a נדה in place of a זבה.

phrases.english: Ravina said: it was ‘a menstruating woman’ that the reciter taught before him:
phrases.notes: This is another way the conversation in Step 30 went.

phrases.english: ‘And a menstruating woman, we slaughter for her on the seventh day.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the exchange in Steps 30-34, with a נדה in place of a זבה. This version then goes through the same cycle: challenge, emendation and a פשיטא objection (Steps 36-39).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate version of the source text (a different case).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא recited before רב אדא בר אהבה was about a זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא was about a נדה.

steps.title: A נדה is not fit on her seventh day
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה objects: a נדה only immerses on the night after her seventh day, and she is not fit until sunset of the eighth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is a נדה fit on the seventh? Even according to the one who says we slaughter and sprinkle for a person impure from a שרץ, that is because he will be fit by evening. But a נדה only immerses on the night after the seventh, and until the eighth day, when sunset passes for her, she is not fit!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה raises the same objection as in Step 31, now about the נדה. On her seventh day she cannot become fit by that evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person impure from a שרץ can immerse that day and be fit by evening, so some allow slaughtering for him. A נדה only immerses on the night after her seventh day. She becomes fully pure at sunset of the eighth day, so on the seventh she is too early.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone made impure by touching a dead creeping creature. He becomes pure that same evening after immersing.
We slaughter (the animal) and sprinkle (its blood).
Sunset that completes purification after immersion.
By evening; at night.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִדָּה בַּשְּׁבִיעִי מִי חַזְיָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: is a menstruating woman fit on the seventh?
Even according to the one who says
we slaughter and sprinkle for one impure from a creeping creature,
that is because he is fit by evening,
but a menstruating woman immerses only on the night after the seventh,
and until the eighth day, when sunset passes for her,
she is not fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִדָּה בַּשְּׁבִיעִי מִי חַזְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא that רבינא quoted in Step 35, the same way Step 31 challenged the זבה version.
steps.kashyaTarget: ‘We slaughter for a נדה on the seventh day.’
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You can only slaughter for someone who will be fit by that evening. A נדה on her seventh day will not be fit until the next day.

steps.title: Correct the text to 'eighth day'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is corrected to say a נדה's eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: ‘on the eighth.’
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it reads 'eighth day.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: On her eighth day, the נדה has already immersed the night before. She will be pure at sunset, so slaughtering for her then works. This mirrors the fix in Step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. This introduces a correction to the text.

phrases.english: Rather, say: ‘on the eighth.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of Step 36 by correcting the text.

steps.title: Why teach the obvious for a נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if we slaughter on the eighth day even for a זבה who still owes a קרבן, then surely we do so for a נדה, who owes none.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! Now, if for a זבה, who is still missing her atonement-offering, we slaughter and sprinkle for her on the eighth day, then for a נדה, who is not missing an atonement-offering, does it need to be said that we slaughter and sprinkle for her?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the corrected ruling for a נדה is obvious. It reasons from the harder case to the easier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זבה is the harder case, because she still has to bring a קרבן, and the משנה still allows slaughtering for her on the eighth. A נדה has no קרבן at all, so she should certainly qualify. So why would a ברייתא bother to state it?

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if even... This opens a 'how much more so' argument from a harder case.
A woman impure from unusual bleeding. She must bring a קרבן on her eighth day.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two women. The זבה owes a קרבן on day eight, while the נדה owes none. That difference is what makes the נדה case seem obvious.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
Now, if a zava, who is still lacking atonement,
we slaughter and sprinkle for her on the eighth day,
then a menstruating woman, who is not lacking atonement,
does it need to be said that we slaughter and sprinkle for her?!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! הַשְׁתָּא וּמָה זָבָה דִּמְיחַסְּרָא כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the corrected text of Step 37 as redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected ברייתא: slaughter for a נדה on her eighth day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already known for the harder case (the זבה). So it obviously applies to the easier case (the נדה), and stating it is unnecessary.

steps.title: The ברייתא mentions a נדה to teach: eighth day yes, seventh day no
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא had to mention a נדה to teach that we slaughter for her on the eighth day but not on the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא needed to mention a נדה. This is what it teaches us: on the eighth day, yes; on the seventh day, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 38. It explains why a נדה had to be mentioned even though a זבה was already covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not the 'eighth day' itself. The point is to exclude the seventh day. We might have thought a נדה is like others whose day of purification is the seventh. The ברייתא says no: for a נדה, nothing can be done for her on the seventh day.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this)
This is what it teaches us (the new point)
On the eighth day, yes
On the seventh day, no

steps.confusionAlert: The new point is the 'NO' about the seventh day, not the 'yes' about the eighth. The 'yes' was already obvious from the זבה case.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him [to teach the case of] a menstruating woman,
this is what it teaches us:
on the eighth [day], yes; on the seventh, no,
phrases.notes: For a נדה, the קרבן פסח may be slaughtered for her only from the eighth day.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִדָּה אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 38, which asked why a נדה needed mentioning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new point (a חידוש): excluding the seventh day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning a נדה adds nothing, since it follows from the זבה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning a נדה teaches that for her the seventh day is excluded; only the eighth works.

steps.title: Most people immerse by day, but a נדה and a יולדת immerse at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the point: all who must immerse do so by day, except a נדה and a יולדת, who immerse at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: All who are obligated to immerse, their immersion is in the daytime. A נדה and a woman after childbirth immerse at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show why the seventh day does not work for a נדה. She cannot immerse during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other impure people can immerse on the daytime of their last day and be pure by evening. That is why, according to the view that allows slaughtering for a טמא שרץ, the קרבן פסח could be slaughtered for them that day. A נדה can only immerse on the night after day seven, so even under that view she cannot be fit by the evening of her seventh day.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Those obligated to immerse in a מקוה
A woman after childbirth
At night

phrases.english: as it was taught: all who are obligated in immersions —
their immersion is in the day;
a menstruating woman and a woman after childbirth — their immersion is at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי טְבִילוֹת טְבִילָתָן בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the 'seventh day, no' rule of step 39.
steps.raayaObject: That a נדה cannot have the קרבן פסח slaughtered for her on her seventh day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: everyone immerses by day except a נדה and a יולדת, who immerse at night.

steps.title: The פסוק source: she stays a נדה for all seven full days
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא derives the nighttime immersion from the פסוק 'seven days she shall be in her impurity.' A יולדת is linked to a נדה by a הקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One might think she may immerse while it is still day. Therefore the verse says, 'Seven days she shall be in her impurity.' She stays in her impurity for all seven days. And a woman after childbirth is compared to a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that explains where the 'night immersion' rule comes from in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'seven days' mean seven complete days. So a נדה cannot immerse on the seventh day, because that would cut the seventh day short. A יולדת gets the same rule, because the תורה compares her to a נדה ('as in the days of her menstrual flow').

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
While it is still day
Therefore the verse says
Is compared (by a הֶקֵּשׁ, a תורה comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: A נדה and a יולדת must finish all seven full days and only then immerse at night. So the קרבן פסח is slaughtered for a נדה only on her eighth day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a נדה immerses only at night after her days are complete.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא טוֹבֶלֶת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם?
phrases.english: As it was taught: I might think she may immerse while it is still day?
Therefore the verse states:
"Seven days she shall be in her impurity" (ויקרא טו:יט) —
she shall be in her impurity all seven [full days].
And a woman after childbirth is compared to a menstruating woman.
phrases.notes: From ויקרא יב:ב: 'as in the days of her menstrual flow.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא טוֹבֶלֶת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the rule cited in step 40.
steps.raayaObject: That a נדה and a יולדת immerse only at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'שבעת ימים תהיה בנדתה' (seven full days), plus a הקש linking a יולדת to a נדה.

steps.title: A new משנה opens with the case of a mourner
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins, introducing the case of an אונן (a mourner on the day a close relative died).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The acute mourner,
steps.whatsHappening: The previous discussion is finished, and a new משנה begins. Only its first word appears here; the rest continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן is a person on the day a close relative died. On that day he may not eat קדשים. The משנה is setting up whether such a person can still take part in the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A mourner on the day of a close relative's death

phrases.english: MISHNA: The acute mourner,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the נדה/זבה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of an אונן regarding the קרבן פסח. The ruling continues on the next amud.
